reference_traces.rationale: The reviewer identified the work as addressing a key integrin-activation question; the final paper presents direct talin–kindlin binding together with β-tail allostery as the proposed mechanism.

The reviewer requested that differences between β1-CT and β3-CT be considered in interpreting the model. The final paper discusses ternary complexes across tails but the evidence remains centered on the tested systems.
The reviewer credited the affinity analyses, NMR interface mapping and mutagenesis; the final paper documents direct-interaction and functional assays spanning these modalities.
The reviewer highlighted mutation and cell-reconstitution experiments; the final paper reports impaired activation, adhesion and spreading after separating the β1-tail binding sites.

The reviewer questioned apparent Kd values from unsaturated and potentially cooperative measurements. The final paper retains bell-shaped traces, excluded high-concentration observations and extrapolated nonlinear regressions.

The reviewer requested transparent model-generation methods and integration of crosslinking and NMR evidence. The final manuscript supplies the method, but states that the structural model was generated manually because critical structural data are unavailable.

The reviewer requested identification of assignments that could not be reliably transferred. The final paper specifies that only about 47% of KIND2-F0 backbone amide shifts could be transferred, preserving a coverage limitation.

The reviewer found the rationale and comparability of multiple constructs unclear. The final paper explains the molecular-weight and solubility rationale for TLN1-F3 and ΔKIND2, while those minimized constructs remain the basis for key solution-state NMR inferences.

The reviewer asked for residue-specific structural detail of the proposed allosteric network. The final paper reports coupled binding-site effects and perturbation-based experiments, but does not resolve a residue-level network.

The reviewer asked whether the proposed assembly is compatible with compact talin. The final paper juxtaposes cloverleaf and linear talin configurations, leaving the relevant conformational state in the functional complex unresolved.
The reviewer requested construct rationale and kindlin mapping. The final paper explains the minimized NMR constructs and includes KIND2-F0 assignment and mapping information.

The reviewer requested clearer NMR intensity presentation and an average peak-intensity line. The final figure caption reports mean intensities and the final figure description identifies the intensity plots.
The reviewer requested a description of structural-model generation. The final paper provides the source structures, crosslink-distance treatment and manual assembly procedure.
The reviewer requested a clearer MST measurement principle. The final paper describes the pre- and post-laser fluorescence measurements used to minimize heat effects.

limiting_points.suggested_action: Clarify the scope of inference across integrin-tail contexts.
limiting_points.text: The mechanistic advance is bounded by tail-context dependence: the reviewer noted β1-CT and β3-CT differences, while the final discussion situates the model alongside prior ternary-complex observations across β tails.

supporting_points.text: The study advances a specific mechanism for talin–kindlin cooperation by connecting β-tail allostery with a direct talin–kindlin interaction and ternary-complex dynamics.

questions.text: Which residue-level conformational changes form the allosteric network linking the talin- and kindlin-binding regions of β1-CT?

questions.suggested_action: Determine the talin conformation in the functional ternary complex.
questions.text: Does the talin–kindlin interface operate with compact cloverleaf talin, a linear talin-head conformation, or an equilibrium between them in the functional ternary complex?

strengths.text: The evidence integrates NMR, affinity and competition measurements, mutational perturbations and cellular assays rather than relying on a single experimental modality.
Perturbing the direct interaction and separating the adjacent β1-tail binding sites links the proposed molecular coupling to integrin activation, adhesion and spreading phenotypes in cells.

summary.text: This study examines how talin and kindlin cooperate at integrin β tails, proposing that asymmetric tail allostery and direct talin–kindlin binding regulate a dynamic ternary complex. Orthogonal biochemical, structural and cellular experiments support the central mechanism and its functional relevance. Residual limits concern apparent affinity estimates, incomplete structural resolution of the allosteric pathway and interface, partial KIND2 NMR assignment coverage, and the use of minimized constructs in core solution-state measurements.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Quantify the uncertainty and model dependence of affinity estimates.
weaknesses.text: The affinity analysis retains an important interpretive limitation: KIND2 MST traces are bell-shaped at high concentration, some observations are excluded from regression, and reported values include extrapolated estimates. This constrains interpretation of apparent Kd values and cooperativity.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Distinguish the experimentally constrained interface from the manually assembled structural model.
weaknesses.text: The structural model is informative but remains limited because critical structural regions were unavailable and the complex was assembled manually from reported structures and crosslink distances.

weaknesses.suggested_action: State the assignment coverage when interpreting KIND2-F0 maps.
weaknesses.text: KIND2-F0 structural interpretation has incomplete NMR coverage: only about 47% of backbone amide chemical shifts could be transferred, limiting the completeness of residue-level mapping.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Bound conclusions drawn from minimized solution-state constructs.
weaknesses.text: Key NMR experiments use TLN1-F3 and ΔKIND2 constructs selected for molecular weight, solubility and spectral quality. The complementary nanodisc assay helps, but construct-dependent interpretation remains a residual limitation for the full-length membrane-associated system.

revision_ledger.residual_summary: The construct rationale and available KIND2 mapping information are present in the final paper.
The final figure description reports the intensity information requested for visual interpretation.
The final methods describe structural-model generation and the handling of crosslink restraints.
The final paper describes the MST measurement timing used to minimize heat effects.
